user.title: Connect FRITZ!Box
user.description: Credentials of a FRITZ!Box user with the right "FRITZ!Box settings". TR-064 must be enabled under Home Network > Network > Network Settings > "Allow access for applications".

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: The login for the FRITZ!Box {host} no longer works. Enter the current credentials.

reconfigure.title: Change the connection
reconfigure.description: Use this when the FRITZ!Box has a new address. The login stays as it is.

confirm.title: Connect {name}
confirm.description: A FRITZ!Box was found at {host}. Enter the credentials of a user with the right "FRITZ!Box settings". TR-064 must be enabled under Home Network > Network > Network Settings > "Allow access for applications".

error.mesh_repeater: This device is a mesh repeater. Connect to the FRITZ!Box that is the mesh master, only it knows all devices.

abort.wrong_device: This is a different FRITZ!Box than the one that was set up.
abort.ignore_ip6_link_local: The address of the box is an IPv6 link-local address, which cannot be used.
abort.mesh_repeater: This device is a mesh repeater. Set up the FRITZ!Box that is the mesh master; the repeaters are controlled through it.
abort.already_in_progress: The setup of this FRITZ!Box is already in progress.

data.adopt_names: Take over device names from the FRITZ!Box
data.show_vendor: Show the vendor of a device
data.wake_on_lan_wifi: Wake on LAN also for Wi-Fi devices
data.ignore_guests: Ignore devices in the guest network
data.ignore_private_macs: Ignore devices with a private (randomized) MAC address
data.skip_offline: Do not create devices for offline hosts
data.stale_repair: Notify about devices offline for long
data.stale_days: Days offline before a device counts as gone

data_description.consider_home: How long an offline device still counts as home.
data_description.adopt_names: Names you set yourself in Home Assistant are never overwritten.
data_description.show_vendor: The vendor comes from the MAC address, from a list that ships with Home Assistant; nothing is sent anywhere. It shows as the manufacturer of the device in Home Assistant and in the new device event. The panel shows it whatever this says. Private (randomized) addresses have none. Turning this off does not remove a manufacturer already entered.
data_description.wake_on_lan_wifi: Off by default: a Wi-Fi device in standby mostly does not hear a magic packet, so the button and the automatic Wake on LAN switch are only created for devices not known to sit on Wi-Fi. Turn this on if your Wi-Fi devices wake up (some TVs do). Turning it off does not remove what was created.
data_description.hidden_macs: Devices removed by hand are listed here. Deselect one to show it again.
data_description.skip_offline: The box remembers every device it ever saw. A host that is offline and has no device yet gets one when it first comes online. Existing devices are kept.
data_description.stale_repair: With this on, a repair lists the devices that have been offline longer than the days below and offers to hide them. Nothing is hidden without your choice. Devices without a time on record are left out.

no_ipv4_address.message: The device has no IPv4 address, its internet access cannot be switched.

unknown_profile.message: The access profile is not known to the box.

ip_changed.message: The address of the device changed. Its internet access was not switched, try again after the next update.

no_target.message: The device is not known to this integration or is hidden.

no_write_rights.message: The user of the integration may not change settings.

name_not_writeable.message: The name of {name} cannot be changed in the FRITZ!Box.

vpn_unknown.message: The box does not know this VPN connection, or it cannot be changed.

vpn_not_changed.message: The box did not switch the VPN connection.

route_unknown.message: The box has no static route to {network}.

route_not_changed.message: The box did not switch the route.

route_invalid_network.message: That is not a network address. Use the form 10.8.0.0/24, with the network address in front of the slash.

route_all_traffic.message: A route for everything (0.0.0.0/0) is not allowed: it would redirect the internet.

route_overlaps_home.message: The destination overlaps the home network or contains the box. The traffic would stay in the home network.

route_invalid_gateway.message: The gateway is not an IPv4 address.

route_gateway_outside.message: The gateway must be a device in the home network.

route_gateway_is_box.message: The gateway must not be the box itself.

route_gateway_in_target.message: The gateway must not be inside the destination network.

route_invalid_metric.message: The metric must be a whole number from 0 to 65535.

route_duplicate.message: The box already has a route to this network. Delete it first or switch it.

route_home_unknown.message: The box does not tell its home network, so the route cannot be checked.

no_guest_wifi.message: The box has no guest Wi-Fi.

missing_rights.title: Missing rights for the FRITZ!Box user
missing_rights.description: The user "{user}" may not change settings. The devices are shown, but the internet access switches and the Wake on LAN buttons are not created. Give the user the right "FRITZ!Box settings" under System > FRITZ!Box Users.

init.title: Hide devices offline for long
init.description: {count} devices have been offline for more than {days} days. Tick the devices to hide. Hiding them removes their entities; they stay hidden until you show them again in the options.

internet_line.title: The DSL line is weak
internet_line.description: The noise margin of the DSL line has been below 10 dB for over an hour (now {margin} dB). The connection may drop or slow down. Check the cable and the socket, and ask the provider if it stays. The internet page of the FRITZ!Box Network panel shows the line.

mesh_repeater_lost.title: A repeater is missing in the mesh
mesh_repeater_lost.description: The box has not listed {count} repeater(s) in its mesh for a while: {names}. Check the power and the connection of the repeater. The issue goes away when the box lists it again; if it is gone for good, delete its device.

internet_reconnects.title: The internet connection keeps dropping
internet_reconnects.description: The box set up its internet connection {count} times in the last 24 hours. Check the line and the cable, and ask the provider if it continues. The internet page of the FRITZ!Box Network panel shows the events.

set_name.name: Rename device
set_name.description: Renames the device in the FRITZ!Box itself. The name in Home Assistant follows if names are taken over; entity ids never change.

wake_on_lan.name: Wake on LAN
wake_on_lan.description: Sends the Wake on LAN signal of the box to the device.

capture.name: Start packet capture
capture.description: Records the traffic of the box as a pcap. With a device as target only its traffic is kept. The file is in /config/fritzbox_captures and can be downloaded in the panel under Diagnosis.

interface.name: Interface
interface.description: Name of the interface in the box, as on its packet capture page: 1-lan (LAN), 2-1 (1st internet connection), 1-vap0 and 1-vap1 (Wi-Fi). The panel lists them under Diagnosis. For a device choose LAN or Wi-Fi.

size.name: Maximum size
size.description: Megabytes; the recording ends when they are reached.

remove_unavailable_vpn.name: Remove unavailable VPN entities
remove_unavailable_vpn.description: Removes the entities of WireGuard connections that no longer exist on the box, for example after one was deleted or renamed. Does nothing while the box tells no list of connections.

set_route.name: Switch route
set_route.description: Switches a static IPv4 route of the box on or off, for example the route to a second router only while someone is home. The panel lists the routes under Address space > Routes.

network.name: Network
network.description: Destination network of the route as the panel shows it, for example 10.8.0.0/24

enabled.name: On
enabled.description: Whether the route is switched on

set_guest_wifi_password.name: Set guest Wi-Fi password
set_guest_wifi_password.description: Sets the password of the guest Wi-Fi. Without a password a random one is made and returned as the response of the action. This integration does not log the password, but the request to the box shows in the log if debug logging is on for fritzconnection, and the password is part of the data of the action and shows in traces and the event log of Home Assistant if you give one. Devices on the guest network have to log in again.

password.name: Password
password.description: 8 to 63 characters. Leave empty for a random password.

length.name: Length
length.description: Length of the random password, used only if no password is given.
